region: Southern Wairau Valley · Marlborough, New Zealand
about: Deep Down is a small Marlborough label founded by Peter Lorimer and winemaker Clive Dougall, who met while each was looking for a project built around distinctive wine and an ethical, transparent business. Dougall spent twelve years as winemaker at Seresin Estate, where he made Marlborough’s first certified organic wine, and chairs Organic Winegrowers New Zealand. Deep Down became a Certified B Corporation in 2023, and the name is a nod to trusting your gut.

The Sauvignon Blanc comes from a single certified organic vineyard on Ashmore Farm, on the southern side of the Wairau Valley at the foot of the hills, on silt, clay and river gravel. Dougall’s farming leans on compost and biodiversity, and the cellar work is hands-off. In 2024 the wine fermented with the grapes’ own yeasts, about 65% in stainless steel and 35% in old 500-litre barrels, and half went through malolactic fermentation, aiming for a rounder, quieter style than typical Marlborough Sauvignon.

Critics note lemon peel, orange blossom, rose petal and flint on the nose, then a medium-bodied palate with focused acidity, passionfruit and a touch of yeasty, slightly oxidative complexity from the barrels and wild fermentation. Expect yellow plum, yellow apple, honeysuckle and dusty citrus. It is a Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc for guests who find the region’s usual style too loud.
facts: Ashmore Farm, single vineyard, southern Wairau Valley
Wild-yeast fermentation; ~65% stainless steel, 35% old 500 L barrels; 50% malolactic
